questions.question: Classify the types of pasteurization based on temperature and time. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Classify the types of pasteurization based on temperature and time.
  • • Pasteurization is the process of heating foods, mainly liquids, to destroy pathogenic
  • microorganisms without affecting the nutritional and sensory qualities.
  • • Based on temperature and time, pasteurization is classified as:
  • o Low Temperature Long Time (LTLT): Heating at 63°C for 30 minutes –
  • commonly used for milk and liquid foods.
  • o High Temperature Short Time (HTST): Heating at 72°C for 15 seconds – rapid
  • process ensuring microbial destruction while maintaining flavor.
  • o Ultra High Temperature (UHT): Heating at 135–150°C for 1–2 seconds –
  • sterilizes product for long shelf life without refrigeration.
  • • The choice depends on product type, microbial load, and desired shelf life.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Describe the different types of membranes used in food applications. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the different types of membranes used in food applications.
  • o Membrane separation processes are used for concentration, purification, and fractionation
  • of food materials.
  • o Major types include:
  • o Microfiltration (MF): Pore size 0.1–10 µm; removes suspended solids and
  • bacteria.
  • o Ultrafiltration (UF): Pore size 0.001–0.1 µm; separates proteins and
  • macromolecules.
  • o Nanofiltration (NF): Pore size 0.0001–0.001 µm; removes salts and small
  • organics.
  • o Reverse Osmosis (RO): Smallest pores; removes water from solutions for
  • concentration.
  • • Applications include whey protein concentration, juice clarification, and water
  • purification.

questions.question: Discuss the effect of food additives on human health. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the effect of food additives on human health.
  • • Food additives enhance flavor, appearance, texture, and shelf life of foods.
  • • Positive effects:
  • o Preservatives prevent spoilage and extend shelf life.
  • o Antioxidants reduce oxidation and maintain nutritional quality.
  • o Fortifying agents improve nutritional value.
  • • Negative effects:
  • o Excess artificial additives may cause allergies or hyperactivity in children.
  • o Some synthetic colorants and preservatives may have carcinogenic potential if
  • misused.
  • • Regulatory agencies (FSSAI, FDA) set safe limits for additive use to protect consumers.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Interpret the role of temperature in food preservation. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Interpret the role of temperature in food preservation.
  • • Temperature is a factor controlling microbial growth, enzyme activity, and chemical
  • reactions in food.
  • • Low temperature preservation:
  • o Refrigeration (0–5°C) slows microbial activity and enzyme reactions.
  • o Freezing (-18°C or lower) halts microbial growth by converting water into ice.
  • • High temperature preservation:
  • o Pasteurization and sterilization destroy pathogenic and spoilage microorganisms.
  • o Blanching inactivates enzymes before freezing or canning.
  • • Proper temperature control ensures food safety and retains sensory and nutritional
  • quality.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: A food label shows E330. Apply your knowledge to identify the additive and explain its role in foods. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• A food label shows E330. Apply your knowledge to identify the additive and explain its role
  • in foods.
  • • E300-E400 comes under Antioxidant
  • • E330 is the code for Citric Acid, a natural organic acid widely used in food processing.
  • • It is obtained naturally from citrus fruits or produced by fermentation of sugars using
  • Aspergillusniger.
  • Functions:
  • • Acts as an acidulant to control pH and impart a tart flavor.
  • • Serves as an antioxidant by chelating metal ions and preventing oxidation.
  • • Enhances the effectiveness of preservatives like sodium benzoate.
  • • Used in beverages, jams, jellies, and fruit juices to maintain flavor and color.
  • Safe within prescribed limits; excessive intake may cause dental erosion.
  • Role of E330 (Citric Acid) in Foods:
  • • Acidulant::Maintains the desired acidity (pH) in foods and beverages.Provides a
  • refreshing sour or tangy taste that enhances flavor.
  • • Preservative:Inhibits the growth of spoilage microorganisms by lowering the pH.,Extends
  • the shelf life of fruit juices, jams, and sauces.
  • • Antioxidant:Acts as a chelating agent that binds metal ions (like iron and copper) which
  • catalyze oxidation.
  • • Flavor Enhancer and Stabilizer:Balances sweetness and sourness in beverages and
  • confectionery.Helps retain color, texture, and aroma during processing and storage.
  • • Synergistic Effect with Other Additives:Boosts the effectiveness of other preservatives
  • such as sodium benzoate and sorbates.

questions.question: Explain physical methods of sterilization / [CO1] [5x4 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain physical methods of sterilization.
  • • Sterilization is the process of destroying all microorganisms, including spores, to ensure
  • food safety.
  • • Physical methods include:
  • o Heat sterilization: Using moist heat (autoclaving) or dry heat (hot air oven) to
  • destroy microbes.
  • o Filtration: Physically removing microorganisms from liquids using membrane
  • filters.
  • o Radiation: Gamma rays or UV rays used to sterilize packaged or surface foods.
  • o High-pressure processing (HPP): Inactivates microbes without heat, preserving
  • nutrients.
  • • These methods ensure microbial safety while maintaining product quality depending on
  • application.
  • ( 4x 5 marks=20)

questions.question: Elaborate the principle, process, equipment and application of food irradiation in preservation / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Elaborate the principle, process, equipment and application of food irradiation in preservation.
  • • Food irradiation is a process of exposing food to controlled ionizing radiation such as
  • gamma rays, X-rays, or electron beams to destroy microorganisms, insects, and parasites.
  • • Principle: Radiation breaks the DNA of microorganisms and insects, preventing
  • reproduction and growth, thus extending shelf life without raising temperature.
  • • Types of radiation: Gamma rays (Cobalt-60, Cesium-137), X-rays, and Electron beams
  • from linear accelerators.
  • • Process: Packed food is passed through an irradiation chamber and exposed to a
  • controlled radiation dose (measured in kGy).
  • • Equipment: Gamma irradiator, linear accelerator, and conveyor systems are used for
  • uniform exposure.
  • • Radiation dose categories: Low dose (up to 1 kGy) for disinfestation, Medium (1–10
  • kGy) for pathogen reduction, High (>10 kGy) for sterilization.
  • • Applications: Control insects in grains, delay ripening, reduce pathogens in meat, sterilize
  • ready-to-eat foods.
  • • Advantages: Extends shelf life, maintains freshness, safe and residue-free process.
  • • Limitations: High equipment cost, slight vitamin loss, and consumer misconceptions
  • about radiation safety.
  • • Safety: Approved by WHO, FAO, and FSSAI when used within prescribed limits.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the importance of antioxidants and their classification in food processing. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the importance of antioxidants and their classification in food processing.
  • • Antioxidants are compounds that delay or prevent oxidation of fats, oils, and vitamins in
  • foods.
  • • They prevent rancidity, maintain color and flavor, protect nutrients, and extend shelf life.
  • • Mechanism: Antioxidants donate hydrogen or electrons to free radicals, terminating
  • oxidation chain reactions.
  • • Classification by source: Natural (ascorbic acid, tocopherols, rosemary extract) and
  • Synthetic (BHA, BHT, TBHQ).
  • • Classification by function: Primary antioxidants stop oxidation chain; Secondary ones
  • chelate metals or decompose peroxides.
  • • Common natural antioxidants: Vitamin C (E300), Vitamin E (E306–309), carotenoids,
  • and flavonoids.
  • • Synthetic antioxidants: Used in bakery, snacks, margarine, and frying oils for stability.
  • • Effectiveness depends on temperature, pH, oxygen, and concentration.
  • • Health aspects: Natural antioxidants are beneficial; synthetic types must follow ADI
  • limits.
  • • Regulated by FSSAI/FAO/WHO Codex to ensure safe use levels.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Describe different types of microbial spoilage. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe different types of microbial spoilage.
  • • Microbial spoilage is food deterioration caused by bacteria, yeasts, and molds.
  • • Major microbes: Bacteria (Bacillus, Clostridium), Yeasts (Saccharomyces, Candida),
  • Molds (Aspergillus, Penicillium).
  • • Cereal foods: Mold growth and musty odor due to storage fungi.
  • • Fruits and vegetables: Soft rot, mold growth, and fermentation by yeasts.
  • • Meat and fish: Putrefaction, slime, and off-odors caused by proteolytic bacteria.
  • • Milk: Sour curdling and gas production by lactic acid bacteria.
  • • Yeast spoilage: Sugar fermentation leading to CO₂ and alcohol in juices and syrups.
  • • Mold spoilage: Surface growth producing toxins and color changes under aerobic
  • conditions.
  • • Factors influencing spoilage: Temperature, pH, moisture, and oxygen.
  • • Prevention: Proper heat treatment, refrigeration, dehydration, and hygiene.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the reasons behind the food dehydration / [CO1] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the reasons behind food dehydration.
  • • Dehydration removes moisture from food to inhibit microbial and enzymatic activity.
  • • Purpose: Extends shelf life, reduces weight and volume for easy storage and transport.
  • • Principle: Reduction of water activity prevents microbial spoilage and enzyme reactions.
  • • Reasons: Prevent microbial growth, inactivate enzymes, and concentrate solids for
  • convenience.
  • • Methods: Sun drying, hot air drying, spray drying, freeze drying, drum drying, vacuum
  • drying.
  • • Quality effects: Proper dehydration retains nutrients, while overheating may cause color
  • loss.
  • • Advantages: Lightweight, low-cost storage, long shelf life, and lower transportation cost.
  • • Factors affecting rate: Air temperature, humidity, airflow velocity, and food size.
  • • Applications: Used in dried fruits, vegetables, milk powder, instant coffee, and soups.
  • • Conclusion: Dehydration is a safe, economical preservation method ensuring longer shelf
  • stability.
  • ( 2x10 marks=20)
